item.title: Xi: National rejuvenation is unstoppable
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-01
Xi: National rejuvenation is unstoppable President applauds PRC's remarkable achievements at reception in Beijing President Xi Jinping said on Wednesday that the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation is unstoppable and expressed full confidence in the bright prospects for Chinese modernization, on the eve of China's National Day on Oct 1. Xi, who is also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks while addressing a reception at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing to celebrate the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China. Xi said that the system of socialism with Chinese characteristics has demonstrated tremendous strengths through long-term exploration and practice, and that China has continued to make progress in modernizing its system and capacity for governance. Reflecting on the past 77 years, Xi said the Party has united and led the Chinese people in tireless efforts, creating the twin miracles of rapid economic development and long-term social stability. China has achieved its first centenary goal of building a moderately prosperous society in all respects and is forging ahead toward its second centenary goal of building a great modern socialist country in all respects, he said. "At this moment, we are immensely proud of the remarkable achievements of New China and fully confident in the bright prospects for Chinese modernization," Xi told around 800 Chinese and foreign guests, including Party and State leaders, foreign envoys, recipients of national honors and dignitaries from all walks of life. Reviewing this year's progress, Xi said the entire Party and the nation have forged ahead with determination and worked tirelessly, formulating and implementing the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-30), making solid progress across various fields, and effectively responding to risks and challenges. The Chinese economy has continued to advance despite pressures, making progress in innovation-led and high-quality development while demonstrating strong resilience and vitality, he said. New progress and achievements have been made in the cause of the Party and the country, Xi added. Facing complex international and domestic conditions, Xi called for adhering to the general principle of pursuing progress while ensuring stability, fully and faithfully applying the new development philosophy on all fronts, and moving faster to foster a new pattern of development. He urged further deepening reform and opening-up, better coordinating development and security, and promoting continued economic improvement through innovation and higher-quality development. Efforts should also be made to guarantee and improve people's livelihoods, meet the targets and tasks set for the year and ensure a good start to the 15th Five-Year Plan period, he said. Xi stressed the need to unswervingly implement the policy of "one country, two systems", under which the people of Hong Kong administer Hong Kong and the people of Macao administer Macao, both with a high degree of autonomy. He called for supporting Hong Kong and Macao in better integrating into and contributing to the country's overall development, and maintaining their long-term prosperity and stability. On cross-Strait relations, Xi called for deepening exchanges and cooperation, resolutely cracking down on "Taiwan independence" separatist forces and opposing external interference. He also urged efforts to promote the peaceful development of cross-Strait relations and advance the cause of national reunification. On foreign affairs, Xi called for adhering to an independent foreign policy of peace, advancing the implementation of the four global initiatives and promoting the building of a community with a shared future for humanity, in order to inject more certainty and positive energy into a world marked by change and turmoil. "As long as we remain confident, stay focused on our goals and move forward steadily, step by step, success will surely belong to the great Communist Party of China, the great Chinese people and the great People's Republic of China," he said. mojingxi@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Tehran says it received official US response
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-01
Tehran says it received official US response Diplomatic efforts gaining traction as mediators try to avoid wider instability Iranian authorities said on Wednesday they received the official US response to their proposal to end the Middle East conflict, state media reported, days after US President Donald Trump rejected the plan. "At today's cabinet meeting, the American side's proposal was presented to President Masoud Pezeshkian by Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi," government spokeswoman Fatemeh Mohajerani told the official IRNA news agency, without specifying the content of the reply. "We will make every effort to bring the agreement to fruition and will firmly stand up for the rights of the Iranian people," Pezeshkian said. "The agreement must now be based on a win-win strategy." Diplomatic efforts gained traction on the sidelines of last week's United Nations General Assembly in New York. Iran said it has put forward seven conditions for ending hostilities and reopening the strategic Strait of Hormuz, a vital route for oil and gas exports. It put forward a peace proposal featuring a seven-day timeline to reopen the strait and pause hostilities. Still, the two sides have yet to strike a deal to reopen the strategic waterway, through which 20 percent of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas flowed before fighting erupted in late February. Trump previously rejected the proposal, prompting ongoing Qatari shuttle diplomacy. Qatar said on Tuesday that meetings and contacts aimed at bridging differences between the United States and Iran are continuing, with Doha exchanging messages between the two sides and seeking to build common ground toward a peaceful settlement. Majed Al Ansari, spokesman for Qatar's Foreign Ministry, said at the ministry's weekly media briefing that a number of meetings and exchanges of messages had taken place in recent days, including meetings in New York. "The effort now is focused on building common ground between the parties," Al Ansari said. The main disagreement is over the sequencing of the plan, which aims to build trust and return to an enhanced version of a US-Iran memorandum of understanding signed in June, an official briefed on the talks between Araghchi and Qatari mediators told Reuters. During Trump's 2024 campaign, he pledged to wrap up ongoing conflicts, bring down inflation and not launch any new wars. Yet the Iran conflict, which the US launched alongside Israel, has pushed up global fuel costs and fueled wider instability across the Middle East. A recent Reuters/Ipsos poll found only 17 percent of respondents approved of Trump's handling of the cost of living — the top issue US people say will determine how they vote in November. Just 34 percent approved of the strikes on Iran. Trump has said the conflict with Iran will end "very soon" but offered no concrete road map. During a speech in Washington, Trump said Iran is "failing very badly" and reiterated his claim that the country will "not have a nuclear weapon". "That'll be over with very soon," he said. "They will not have a nuclear weapon, and oil prices are going to be tumbling down just like they were before I had to make that little excursion to the Islamic Republic of Iran." Fighting has subsided in recent weeks, though the strikes around the strait continue. Iran's Revolutionary Guards said on Wednesday that they have been striking small vessels that try to pass through the strait. "We have been striking ships for quite some time now — specifically the small vessels I mentioned that attempt to pass," Guards spokesman Hossein Mohebi told state TV. The US, meanwhile, has stepped up its economic warfare against Iran, imposing sanctions on Iranian airlines. Oil prices climb Global oil prices climbed on Wednesday after Trump ruled out easing sanctions on Iran. Brent crude futures rose more than 1.1 percent to $103.73 in morning trade, on track for a monthly gain of roughly 14 percent — its steepest monthly rise since July. Authorities in the United Arab Emirates on Wednesday announced the country's gasoline and diesel prices for October, with gas set to rise by as much as 16.6 percent month-on-month. Meanwhile, fighting in Yemen has intensified across the southwestern part of the country after the Houthi group seized the strategic port city of Mocha and Mayyun Island in the Bab al-Mandab Strait earlier last month. The Houthis said on Tuesday that Saudi warplanes carried out 35 airstrikes across five Yemeni provinces over the past 24 hours, as fighting continued between the Houthis and Yemeni government forces on several fronts. Saudi Arabia has yet to comment on the latest Houthi claims. Agencies and Xinhua contributed to this story. Contact the writers at cuihaipei@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Burnham hints at EU return for UK
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-01
Burnham hints at EU return for UK The United Kingdom's Prime Minister Andy Burnham has opened the door to the country rejoining the European Union sooner, rather than later, after saying that Brexit, the process of leaving the 27-member bloc following a referendum in 2016, had "done more harm than good" and that he did not want to leave the issue of the nation's relationship with its neighbors "hanging". Burnham made the initial comment about Brexit not working on Tuesday, during his first Labour Party conference speech since taking over as party leader and prime minister in the summer. He followed up on the remark during a BBC interview the next day. The UK voted in the 2016 referendum by a margin of 52 percent to 48 percent to leave the EU. The fall-out from that decision was the overwhelmingly dominant issue in British politics until the COVID-19 pandemic of 2020, which coincidentally began a matter of weeks after the long, drawn-out process of Brexit was formally signed off. A decade later, the social and economic consequences of the decision to leave the EU still provoke strong opinions on both sides of the debate and Burnham said he wanted clarity on "where we want Britain to go in the next decade". When pushed specifically on whether he wanted the UK to rejoin, a position he has previously publicly backed, he said he wanted to "look at the options". "We could stay as we are. That's definitely an option, if people think this is the right place to stay," he said. "We could look at what (former Conservative Party chancellor of the exchequer) George Osborne has said about a customs union, we could look at what the Liberal Democrats said at their conference about the single market, or we could go all the way. So, there are clearly options that need to be considered, and we have to look at what is doable and what would be the pros and cons of each." Alex Burghart, the Conservative Party's shadow secretary of state for Northern Ireland, accused Burnham of going back on his word, adding "just a few weeks ago, he said he wanted to move on from the Brexit arguments and now he is dragging Britain back into them by floating the prospect of rejoining the EU… while (Labour) look backwards, the Conservatives will look forwards". Ed Davey, leader of the Liberal Democrats, urged Burnham to take bolder action, saying: "Talk is cheap. Burnham must stop with all the 'maybes' and get negotiating that better deal for Britain today." Writing in The New World newspaper in December 2025, Peter Kellner, founder of the YouGov polling service, said that if a referendum were to be held again, the demographic change — including people who have died since 2016 and newly-eligible voters, plus those who would vote differently — would see the majority decision to leave wiped out. "The combined impact of demographics and changed minds is to convert a 1.3 million majority for leaving the EU into an 8.1 million majority for rejoining it," he said. "Even the greatest landslide election victories have come nowhere close to this lead in the popular vote."

item.title: Music maestro eager to wow Chinese audiences
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-01
Music maestro eager to wow Chinese audiences Six's 'brilliant message', 'relevance' praised One of the most high-profile Chinese-born figures in British theater says she is thrilled by the prospect of taking one of the West End's most popular shows to audiences across China this fall. Six the Musical is an international award-winning pop music retelling of the stories of the six wives of England's King Henry VIII, which over the course of a decade has grown from a student project at the Edinburgh Festival Fringe to playing to full houses across Europe, the United States, Asia, and Australia, and that had a six-week run in Shanghai last summer. In early October, the play starts a 12-week tour of China that will take it to Beijing, Chengdu, Guangzhou, Hangzhou, Ningbo, and Suzhou. The show's on-stage musical director, Dalian-born Zhang Yutong, divides her time between working in the world of theater in the United Kingdom and in Shanghai. "I can't tell you how happy I was to take the show to Shanghai last year, as it's where my professional career began – I call it my other life, as I run a theater company there, I write musicals and a do a lot of producing," she said. "I know how much people loved it and how much they want to see it in their local theaters, so it's great that they can see it in their home towns without having to buy a plane ticket – it means so much to the whole theater community, which in China is predominantly young women. As well as that, all the cast and company are so excited about traveling around the country and getting the authentic Chinese experience." Although she has had a lifelong passion for musical theater, Zhang has, by her own admission, taken an unconventional route to her career, being active in student drama while studying linguistics at University College London, but only being alerted to musical direction as a career possibility when a friend studied a master's degree in the subject. After studying at the Royal Conservatoire of Scotland, she worked in Shanghai for two years, then on her return to the UK worked in drama schools around the country before meeting Six's composers, Toby Marlow and Lucy Moss, on another show of theirs, and ending up as musical director of Six's British touring company, and now for the China tour. The show's set-up is the six wives as members of a girl band, each with their own distinctive musical style and appearance, arguing amongst themselves as to who was the most mistreated wife, before realizing that six women working together as one is more powerful than the man who has, for centuries, historically defined them. The musical runs for 80 minutes with no interval and its upbeat, energetic celebratory message of female empowerment and rewriting history as 'herstory' has spawned a huge fan community, known as the Queendom. "It's such a brilliant message – it's been running for almost 10 years but it still remains so relevant, every day people are coming to see it for the first time, attracted by its story and its message," Zhang explained. "There's so much in it, so cleverly packed into quite bite-sized pieces to enjoy in the moment but also to take away – whether or not you see it for the first or 100th time, you can take things away and dwell on it for days. Sometimes, because of how a different actress might deliver a different line, I still find myself going home and thinking about it – that's what continues to attract people to come and see the show." Zhang plays keyboards in the on-stage live band, the Ladies in Waiting, and said that no matter how many times she does the show, the sight of such an energized audience still gives her an emotional lift, particularly in China. "When the curtain opened, I was completely in tears for the first song because I thought 'these are all people who look like me'," she said. The show leans heavily on the multi-member boy band and girl band style of presenting a variety of looks and characters on stage, for audience members to choose the one they identify with, and its Queendom community. Zhang said she knew people whose lives had been changed by seeing it, something she hopes to maintain. "I have friends who can cite Six as one of the reasons they now work professionally in UK theater, because they saw it on holiday in New York, and decided to come and study and work here," she said. "It's fantastic people find it one of their motivators. I've covered (as musical director) for the West End production a few times this year, and at the stage door afterwards, it's always great to see an audience member who is Chinese, I will always have a chat."

item.title: Nation's travel landscape enters new era
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-01
Nation's travel landscape enters new era Relaxed entry policies, digital payments infrastructure prove a magnet for global tourists As a hand-rowing boat drifts across Hangzhou's famed West Lake, Austrian traveler Florian Eisinger finds himself surrounded by willow-lined shores, ancient temples and centuries of history, with the gleaming skyline of one of China's most dynamic cities rising in the distance. For the 23-year-old who was visiting China for the first time in May, the scene captured what surprised him most about the country. "It was probably one of the most mesmerizing countries I visited in my life," Eisinger said. "From the cities to the landscapes to the people, everything was beyond what I had imagined." Two places stood out. "West Lake is just incredible scenery and a lot of history packed into one 'district', all while you have the very modern city of Hangzhou in the background," he said. "I did a boat tour over parts of the lake, and it was jaw-droppingly beautiful." The other place is Shanghai. Some streets, while being nestled within the bustling heart of the metropolis, especially in the evening, are incredibly beautiful, and it is surreal to imagine this being in one of the largest cities in the world, he said.

item.title: What keeps China's high-speed trains so steady?
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-01
What keeps China's high-speed trains so steady? Share - WeChat
A cup of tea can stand upright on a Chinese high-speed train. But the real story isn't the cup. It's the wheel beneath the train. At 350 km/h, the wheel diameter tolerance is tighter than a human hair. Every wheel has its own digital ID. This National Day holiday, millions are traveling home. These wheels carry us safely to our loved ones.

item.title: Leaders pay homage to fallen heroes on Martyrs' Day
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-01
Leaders pay homage to fallen heroes on Martyrs' Day President Xi Jinping and other Party and State leaders attended a ceremony on Wednesday at Tian'anmen Square in central Beijing to present flower baskets to honor fallen national heroes, marking China's 13th Martyrs' Day. Established in 2014 and observed annually on Sept 30, one day before National Day, the day honors those who gave their lives for the liberation of the Chinese people and the nation's development. Since the first observance of Martyrs' Day, Xi, who is also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, has maintained the tradition of paying homage to fallen heroes on this day. On Wednesday morning, Xi and other leaders — Li Qiang, Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang, Li Xi and Han Zheng — joined representatives from all walks of life for the solemn ceremony in front of the Monument to the People's Heroes. At 10 am, all attendees sang the national anthem, followed by a moment of silence in tribute to the fallen heroes. Nine large flower baskets were placed in front of the monument. Xi and other leaders walked up to the foot of the monument, where he straightened the ribbons on the baskets. Then, they walked around the monument to pay tribute. Among the attendees carrying flowers were veterans, relatives of martyrs, recipients of awards and honorary titles, members of ethnic minority groups, students and children. Liu Jia, an associate professor at Beihang University's School of Marxism, watched the live broadcast of the ceremony. He said that observing Martyrs' Day is not only a solemn tribute to fallen heroes, but also a reminder of the hardships and unwavering convictions forged during China's revolutionary struggles. Liu noted that the commemoration came at a key moment, citing that this year marks the 105th anniversary of the founding of the CPC, the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Long March — an epic military trek from 1934 to 1936 that helped lay the foundation for the eventual victory of the Chinese revolution — and the launch of the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-30) for economic and social development. He said that the strength we gain from the Party's glorious history and the Long March will help drive new sci-tech progress today and inspire the younger generation. jihaisheng@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Coo the music, pigeons set city's tone
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-30
Coo the music, pigeons set city's tone Beijing breeders keep tradition of whistling wings, ornamental and racing birds alive In his 1934 essay Autumn in Peiping, writer Yu Dafu described sitting in a courtyard on an autumn morning, looking up at the blue sky and hearing "the sound of domesticated pigeons flying overhead" — part of the unhurried, peaceful rhythm of everyday life in Beijing. Nearly a century later, pigeons are still a defining characteristic of some areas of the city's skyline. On Sept 21, Chinese and foreign guests released white pigeons at a gathering to mark the International Day of Peace. The birds, rising together above the crowd, were a familiar symbol of peace. Similar scenes have unfolded at Tian'anmen Square during National Day celebrations and other major commemorations, when thousands — sometimes tens of thousands — of pigeons have been released above the heart of Beijing. But behind the feathered pageantry is a community with lifelong passion for pigeons and associated traditions. Some of the pigeons released on Sept 21 were raised and trained by Li Xiaolong, a veteran pigeon-keeper from Xicheng district. Li has been around pigeons since he was 3 years old. "I'd hold a pigeon in my hands and play with it," he said. "I was at the pigeon loft almost every day." His love of the birds drew another Beijing boy into the world of pigeons. Ma Chunyu was not yet in kindergarten when he got his first pair of pigeons, taken from beneath the eaves of a neighbor's house. By primary school, his obsession had become difficult for his family to control. "I would secretly take a pigeon to school," Ma recalled. "I'd hide it in my schoolbag, then reach into the book compartment and take it out to stroke it." His mother worried that the birds were keeping him from his homework. Once, when she grabbed a broom and went after his pigeons, Ma wrapped himself around her legs to stop her. When Ma was about 9, he became interested in racing pigeons, which involves training them to return to their home loft from a distant location. "We started at 5 kilometers, then 10 km, and just kept going farther," he said. As a teenager, Ma carried dozens of pigeons in wooden crates, first by bicycle and then by long-distance bus, sometimes traveling more than 80 km before releasing them. "The pigeons got back first — of course they did," he said. "But it took me about two hours." More than half a century later, Ma still keeps pigeons. "When you're upset, you look at them cooing around you, almost like they're talking to you," he said. "Once you see the pigeons, there are no worries." There are fewer places in Beijing today where pigeons can be kept than when Ma was a child. Many courtyard homes and low-rise neighborhoods once suited to pigeon lofts have disappeared or changed. Keeping birds in densely populated residential communities also raises concerns over space, sanitation and disturbance to neighbors. Some longtime pigeon-keepers have moved their birds far from the city center or changed how they raise them, however, several of them told China Daily they now see relatively few young people taking up the pastime.

item.title: Five scenic escapes for the National Day holiday
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-30
Five scenic escapes for the National Day holiday Share - WeChat
From mountain terraces to ancient landmarks and island waters, these five destinations offer inspiration for a National Day holiday getaway, boasting fine mild autumn conditions in early October. Bijie, Guizhou — Music among the terraces In Bijie's Dafang county, the curved terraces of Shexiang Ancient Town resemble a giant fingerprint. The landscape has also become a setting for open-air concerts, with lights tracing the terraces as music fills the night.
